falsifiable_hypothesis: The verified patient-weighted target-union predictor is conservative and stable, while an inner-crossfit targetwise calibration estimates useful additional one-sided correction gain but is too aggressive in one development fold. A fixed symmetry hedge can reduce calibration variance without fold-specific rescue.
safe_component: Exactly reuse the frozen held predictions of patient_weighted_target_union_confidence_js.
aggressive_component: For each outer partition, use only its authenticated three inner whole-patient bandwidth-0.7 OOF prediction tensors at the already-selected spectral option. Build patient-count-weighted contrast shrinkage theta on all three inner folds exactly as in patient_count_weighted_amplitude_js. For each held inner fold k, rebuild theta_-k from the other two inner folds. Let rB_k,j be the equal-patient mean B-orientation OOF residual in held fold k and n_k its patient count. For each target set raw gain g_j=-2*sum_k n_k*theta_-k,j*rB_k,j / sum_k n_k*theta_-k,j^2, defaulting to 1 when the denominator is numerically zero, then clip g_j to [1,3]. Apply qB_aggressive=qB_interpolated_jackknife-0.5*g_j*theta_j; qA_aggressive=qA_loo_bagged.
hedge_rule: For every held sample, target and orientation, q_final=0.5*q_safe+0.5*q_aggressive. The 0.5 hedge is fixed by symmetry before canonical replay. There is no per-fold or per-target hedge weight, no outer-held outcome routing, and no A/B prediction averaging.

task_contract.ab_rule: average losses across separately costed A/B orientations; never average predictions
